claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential combined with molecular dynamics can predict the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach will outperform earlier approaches by capturing atomic-scale complexity and defects.
The applicable material is a bulk crystal that may contain defects and impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Atomic-scale defects and impurities are the structural mediator relevant to the prediction.
Phonon-phonon interactions govern the proposed conductivity mechanism.
Electron-phonon scattering contributes to the proposed conductivity mechanism.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr is predicted to be 5-12 W/(K m) at 300 K.
The proposed approach is expected to improve predictive performance by 20-30% relative to earlier approaches.
Experiments report a total thermal conductivity of 10-17 W/(K m).
The proposed prediction is applicable below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
The accuracy of the machine-learning interatomic potential is uncertain.
The effects of defects and impurities on lattice thermal conductivity are uncertain.
Lattice thermal conductivity should be measured at 100 K, 300 K, and 1000 K.
A deviation greater than 50% from the measured lattice thermal conductivity at any specified temperature falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies only an interatomic potential and molecular dynamics, while the mechanism includes electron-phonon scattering; no electronic model or coupling method is specified to represent that mechanism.
The predicted quantity is lattice-only thermal conductivity, whereas the stated baseline is total thermal conductivity. These are not directly comparable measures of predictive improvement.
